extraction.summary: The authors derive a five-stage background history for one canonical scalar to act as EDE and later dark energy: frozen, transient EDE, rapid depletion, prolonged post-recombination quiescence, and late reactivation. In their tracking-like, quasi-autonomous analysis, a two-slope potential leaves too much scalar energy on the matter-era scaling branch; constant conformal coupling to dark matter cannot lower it enough. They propose an intermediate slope steeper than the EDE slope, followed by a shallow late-time slope. This is a necessary-structure argument within the stated smooth, canonical, approximately constant-slope framework, not a data-qualified model or general no-go theorem.

ideas.title: Unified history requires five separated scalar regimes
ideas.description: The proposed background sequence requires early Hubble freezing, EDE around equality, depletion by recombination, post-recombination quiescence, and reactivation only at low redshift. EDE alters the sound-horizon integral; residual scalar energy changes the broader comoving-distance integral.

equations.definitions: Effective EDE and post-recombination scalar fractions are differently weighted integrals; kernels W_rs and W_χ are defined in text.
equations.domain: First-order perturbation about ΛCDM; schematic reduction and distance-shift estimates.

ideas.title: Two constant-slope regimes retain an excessive matter-era fraction
ideas.description: Radiation tracking fixes λ_early²≈40 for the illustrative Ω_φ≈0.1 EDE level. The same slope gives an uncoupled matter-era scaling fraction 3/λ_early²≈0.075, retaining three quarters of the radiation-era scalar fraction. An early-to-shallow transition skips an independent rapid-depletion regime.

equations.definitions: G is radiation-scaling point; F is matter-scaling point.
equations.domain: Canonical scalar, constant-slope fixed points; values are illustrative.

ideas.title: Constant dark-matter coupling does not sufficiently deplete the scalar
ideas.description: For the baryon-free coupled matter branch, existence imposes a lower bound on β and hence on the residual scalar fraction: its minimum is 3/(2λ_early²), or 3/8 of the radiation-scaling fraction. With the illustrative EDE normalization this is still ≳0.0375. Appendix A argues baryons do not remove the floor; field-dependent couplings are outside the analysis.

equations.definitions: β is constant conformal coupling to cold dark matter; G and F are radiation- and matter-scaling points.
equations.domain: Canonical scalar, constant β, fixed-point/quasi-static analysis; baryonic departures treated perturbatively.

ideas.title: Intermediate steep branch supplies depletion and quiescence
ideas.description: To suppress the matter-era tracking fraction to roughly one percent, the authors require λ_mid²≳300, with λ_mid≫λ_early≫λ_late. The trajectory must turn onto this branch after EDE and before settling on the early-branch matter attractor; exact arrival at the intermediate fixed point is unnecessary in their illustrative trajectory.

equations.definitions: F,mid is the matter-like scaling level on the intermediate branch.
equations.domain: Fixed-point estimate in the canonical tracking framework; order-of-magnitude threshold.

ideas.title: Positive sums of exponentials cannot steepen along increasing field
ideas.description: For positive exponential amplitudes, the effective logarithmic slope is a convex weighted mean of component slopes; its field derivative is minus their weighted variance. It is non-increasing with increasing field and cannot give the required λ_early→λ_mid→λ_late ordering.

equations.definitions: V=Σ_iV_i exp(−λ_iφ), V_i>0; w_i=V_i exp(−λ_iφ)/V, Σ_iw_i=1.
equations.domain: Positive finite sum of fixed-slope exponentials, for evolution toward increasing φ.

ideas.title: A localized shoulder can phenomenologically produce transient steepening
ideas.description: A double-exponential-like potential with a logistic shoulder behaves first with λ_early and later as a sum containing λ_mid=λ_early+n/Δ and λ_late. The authors give n/Δ≈11 as a benchmark and explicitly describe this as phenomenological, not UV-derived.

equations.definitions: n and Δ parameterize shoulder shape and width.
equations.domain: Asymptotic approximations on either side of φ⋆; benchmark λ_early²=40 and λ_mid²=300.

data_dependencies: No new measurements or likelihood analysis. Thresholds are analytical estimates conditioned on cited CMB/BAO/SN constraints and ΛCDM background weighting; trajectories are reported modified-CLASS background integrations. Dataset ancestry, likelihood, priors, chains, and cross-covariance are not provided for those trajectories.
caveats: The phases are necessary background conditions, not sufficient viability conditions; perturbations are not analyzed.

The argument assumes a canonical scalar, smooth rolling depletion by that field, constant conformal coupling β where included, and successive quasi-autonomous regimes with approximately constant logarithmic slope.

Phase transitions, decay, particle production or other dissipation; rapid non-adiabatic slope variations; field-dependent β(φ); noncanonical theories; and disformal couplings are outside the analysis and may evade restrictions.
The shoulder potential is phenomenological, not a UV construction; representative CLASS trajectories do not establish inference or scientific qualification.

usefulness.reason: Provides structured scalar-history requirements, explicit two-slope/coupling obstructions, and a candidate three-slope mechanism for source-level comparison. Assumptions, approximations, perturbation gap, and unqualified background examples warrant independent Sol review before idea acceptance.
